title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Models Is Just Steering
summary: New paper shows 90-96% of RL post-training reward gains in diffusion transformers come from fixed steering vectors using 1.5% of LoRA parameters.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Fixed steering vectors recover 90-96% of RL post-training reward gains in diffusion transformers using just 1.5% of LoRA parameters.
- 288,768-parameter vectors added to frozen Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium replicate what 18.8 million RL-updated parameters achieve.
- Training steering vectors from scratch with Flow-GRPO reaches 50-52% win rate against fully RL-tuned models in user studies.


A research paper published November 19, 2026, challenges the conventional understanding of reinforcement learning in image generation. Researchers from fal, Georgia Tech, IBM Research, and Virginia Tech demonstrate that 90.0 to 96.3% of RL[post-training](https://emergent.sh/glossary/post-training) reward gains across six image diffusion transformers can be recovered using fixed, input-independent steering vectors added to frozen base models. The technique uses approximately 1.5% of the parameters required by a rank-32 LoRA adaptation.


## Parameter Efficiency at Scale


The core finding centers on Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium, where 288,768 parameters added as constant offsets to a frozen model reproduce roughly 90% of what Flow-GRPO reinforcement learning achieves by updating 18.8 million parameters. These per-block steering vectors operate without touching base weights, suggesting that RL post-training primarily steers generation toward outputs the base model already encodes rather than teaching fundamentally new capabilities.


The vectors remain effective across resolutions and transfer between different image sizes. Testing on six RL-tuned image models and two video models, the authors report recovery rates of 89.8 to 111.9% on video tasks, indicating the approach generalizes beyond still images.


## Training From Scratch Matches Full RL


When trained from initialization using Flow-GRPO directly on steering vectors rather than fitting them to an existing RL-tuned model, the method delivers 103.6% of the original RL PickScore gain and 104.6% of OCR metric improvement. A user study comparing outputs shows the steered model achieves a 50 to 52% win rate against fully RL-tuned models, reaching statistical parity.


The authors argue that joint attention mechanisms convert the constant steering shifts into prompt-dependent outputs. The base generator handles prompt-specific work, while RL adjustments primarily nudge the system toward preferred outputs already within its latent capability space.


## Limits and Compute Requirements


The technique shows boundaries in supervised fine-tuning contexts. On DreamBooth subject-fidelity tasks, steering vectors recover only 68 to 95% of similarity metrics, trailing same-size LoRA adaptations at 81 to 100%. Computational overhead remains significant, with fitting the full vector set requiring up to 17 H100-GPU-hours per image model and up to 70 hours for video models.


The appendix notes these costs make the approach most practical for research settings or deployment scenarios where parameter count matters more than one-time training expense. Organizations working with memory-constrained inference pipelines gain the most immediate benefit.


## Release Date


The paper titled "RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is[Activation Steering](https://emergent.sh/glossary/activation-steering) " was officially released on November 19, 2026, on arXiv and Hugging Face. The research arrives during a week of parameter-efficient post-training results, following CurvDelta's low-curvature weight-update work published November 18.


## What This Means


This research reframes reinforcement learning in diffusion models as a steering problem rather than a learning problem. If 90% of reward gains come from adding fixed offsets rather than weight updates, practitioners may reconsider expensive full-model[RL fine-tuning](https://emergent.sh/glossary/rl-fine-tuning) . The 1.5% parameter footprint opens deployment paths for resource-constrained environments, though the upfront compute cost and supervised task limitations prevent universal adoption. For researchers, the work suggests base diffusion transformers already contain most capabilities RL appears to teach, raising questions about where model capacity actually bottlenecks quality improvements.
